recfVFnXBwRsp6WLY.Bio: Steven A. Young holds an MSci and a PhD in theoretical physics, and now describes himself as an author, musician and natural philosopher. He is the author of A Fool's Wisdom: Science Conspiracies & The Secret Art of Alchemy, which critiques scientific materialism before presenting Hermetic alchemy as a science of transformation. Under the alias Hedflux he has produced electronic music since 2003, going full time in 2010 and founding the label Luminus Music, with a body of work collected in a 20 Year Legacy Collection of 88 tracks and 12 DJ mixes. He lives in Scotland, where he teaches Audio Alchemy, a synthesis of musical, scientific and Hermetic knowledge.
recfVFnXBwRsp6WLY.Name: Steven Young

recl1wvjyRP3XfBBu.Bio: Marty Leeds is a gematria researcher, author and preacher who founded The Gnostic Church and Academy of Lord Jesus Christ in 2022, where he serves as head teacher and spiritual leader. A working minister since 2011, he is the author of more than ten books, among them the Pi & The English Alphabet series, Scripture in the Stars, The Keys to the Tarot and Gnosticism Defined: The Tenets of The Order, built around a mathematical cipher he says is hidden beneath the English alphabet. His teaching centers on Prisca Theologia, the idea of a single wisdom underlying the world's religions, drawing together gematria, Kabbalah, astrology and comparative mythology. He streams weekly sermons free through the Gnostic Academy's YouTube and Rumble channels.
recl1wvjyRP3XfBBu.Name: Marty Leeds

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title":"Nobody Has Seen An Atom","body":"Young says his doubts began after investigating virus claims, when he went looking for anyone who works directly with individual atoms and could not find them; physicists, he argues, run experiments, plot data on graphs, and then treat a small bump in the graph as proof of a particle, while the foundational experiments are rarely repeated or verified. Garton notes that mainstream science holds atoms to be smaller than a wavelength of light, so light supposedly bends around them rather than revealing them. Leeds adds that ion based microscopes assume atomic theory in order to test atomic theory, which he calls a circular conflict."},{"title":"Quantity Cannot Make Quality","body":"Young asks how a water molecule, an abstract diagram with no wetness of its own, produces the wetness of water, and takes the question to the periodic table: hydrogen, helium, and lithium differ by single protons, yet adding one proton supposedly turns a transparent rising gas into a soft metal dug out of rock, and gold sits right beside mercury. Garton draws on Rene Guenon's The Reign of Quantity and the Signs of the Times, arguing that qualities and essences exist before physical matter in a Platonic sense, so no count of protons could ever generate them."},{"title":"Small Stuff And Nonsense","body":"Young maps particle physics onto what he sees as an inverted alchemy: the God particle at the top, then quark and lepton, then proton, neutron, and electron, then the four states of matter, mirroring the tetractys that descends from a godhead through three principles to the four elements. He notes lepton comes from the Greek lepta, meaning tiny, while quark is a German colloquialism for something trivial, so the story tells people they are built from small stuff and nonsense. Both men read this as deliberate diminishment; Leeds calls the theories mind spells and urges seeking provable theorems instead."},{"title":"A Science Without Fruits","body":"Young cites Cambridge physicist David Tong telling the Royal Institution that particles do not exist and that everything comes from vibrations in a fluid medium, though Tong then keeps the same particles as fields. He contrasts the sprawling standard model equation with music theory, which yields endless songs, and says the God particle rests on a faint bump in a graph. Leeds applies the test of fruits to CERN, nanotech, and gene testing, calling DNA matching a database of names. Garton argues such projects also burn off surplus debt based currency while quietly feeding surveillance."},{"title":"Squaring The Circle Of Elements","body":"Young notes that Mendeleev's first table was an eight by eight grid whose opening element was the ether, called Newtonium after Newton, removed around 1905, and that the modern table lists calculated atomic masses derived from Avogadro's number rather than measured substances. Leeds argues the genuine periodic arrangement is a circle, the zodiac, so turning it into a table literally squared the circle and made spiritual things material. He ties earth, air, water, and fire to 78 in his gematria, the twelfth triangular number, matching the tarot's 22 major and 56 minor cards."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Nobody has ever seen an atom. Physics PhD Dr. Steven Young (Hedflux) and Marty Leeds of the Gnostic Academy put atomic theory and particle physics on trial. No direct observation, no repeatable experiment, no proof. In this episode we work through what the evidence for atoms actually consists of: bumps on graphs, microscopes that presuppose the atoms they claim to reveal, and a mind-spell to make you feel small. From there the conversation widens into the periodic table that is not periodic, the one proton that supposedly turns gold into mercury, Mendeleev's erased ether, the boondoggle economics of CERN, and the older map the moderns replaced: earth, air, water, fire, and the living ether.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Elements Are Written Into Genesis", "body": "Marty reads the opening lines of Genesis as a plain statement of the elements, with time, the heaven and the earth as the up force and the down force, the spirit moving over the waters and then the command for light, so that earth, air, water and fire and the ether are all present before anything is said about particles. The Big Bang, on this reading, is an inversion of something that actually happened. Steven comes at it from the other end and admits that alchemy is what sent a physicist back to scripture in the first place."}, {"title": "Health Makes Sense in Four Humors", "body": "Steven describes trying to picture his own body after a physics PhD, imagining atoms suspended in space and a piece fallen off a molecule whenever he felt pain, until he realised that physicists are not physicians. The four humors gave him a working model instead: one river entering by the mouth, split at the liver into blood, yellow bile, black bile and phlegm, with the spent black bile cycled back and stored in the spleen to drive hunger. Chance adds the biofield reading of the liver, where anger is simply the other face of care."}, {"title": "There Is No Smallest Thing", "body": "Chance lays out the objection that never gets answered. Any mass occupies space, and anything extended in space is infinitely divisible, the way a number line keeps splitting between zero and one, so an ultimate indivisible particle contradicts itself before a single experiment is run. Indivisibility belongs to the unity of spirit, he argues, and has been pasted onto the lowest level of the corporeal realm. Steven follows the same thread into point particles, the Planck length and quantized space, and calls the photon a fallacy that hands the priesthood of light to physicists."}, {"title": "The Void Is Metaphysically Incoherent", "body": "If atoms are real, something has to hold them, and modern physics offers empty space. Chance answers that a container without content is not a container, so the very stage atomism needs cannot exist. Steven traces the same loss historically, with the ether removed as a continuous all pervading medium and the vacuum installed in its place, and compares it to the nothing that consumes the world in The NeverEnding Story. He finds the anagrams of ether pointing at heart, earth and hearth, and concludes that the ether is where we came from and what we return to."}, {"title": "Quantity Is Not the Same as Quality", "body": "Guenon supplies the frame. Counting is discontinuous, five separate apples in a basket, while measuring is continuous, an unbroken stretch that can always be divided further, and a science built entirely on quantity treats the two as one thing. Chance argues that number is metaphysical and that measurement is how we apply number to something that is not a number, so atomism never discovered countable units, it requires them. Marty asks where number itself came from in a purely physical creation, and Steven regrets years of trigonometry that never once mentioned phi."}]
